issue_context.title: [habitica] API_CALL: User 'xxx' not configured
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I can't get the habitica.api_call service to work. Whenever I try to run the service, I get this error in the logs:

`2021-06-22 18:30:48 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.habitica] API_CALL: User 'matt' not configured`

I've tried setting the _name_ in the service to my username set in HA, my Habitica username, and random strings, but I always get the same error in the logs. I've tried setting the name when first adding the integration and using that, and leaving it blank to be defaulted. 

Am I missing something obvious or is this broken?

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

habitica

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/habitica/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: habitica.api_call
data:
  name: matt
  path:
    - tasks
    - user
    - post
  args:
    text: Use API from Home Assistant
    type: todo
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-06-22 18:30:48 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.habitica] API_CALL: User 'matt' not configured
```


### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @asmfreak, @leikoilja, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`habitica`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L195) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hmm.. As I can see [this line](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6814e9607adfbc67c3b73dd4d45b3c53c7ee4041/homeassistant/components/habitica/__init__.py#L148) is the source of this bug. Recent change by @leikoilja in the initialization made the key in domain  `entry.entry_id`. This change broke in turn [this line](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6814e9607adfbc67c3b73dd4d45b3c53c7ee4041/homeassistant/components/habitica/__init__.py#L114). As it is expecting `name`, not `entry.entry_id`.
Amazing, thanks for taking a look and fixing it, @ASMfreaK 💥 🚀
